title: Rabbi Redifa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was Rabbi Yonah’s student, as in Jerusalem Talmud Peah 4:5, where he said: “Rabbi Yonah and Rabbi Yose disagreed.”
He spoke in Rabbi Yonah’s name, as in Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim, beginning of chapter 8; Yevamot 1:2; Ketubot, chapter 7, end of halakhah 7; and Kiddushin, chapter 2, end of halakhah 4.
We likewise find in Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 6:1: “Rabbi Adifa, Rabbi Acha in the name of Rabbi Bun bar Kahana.”
In Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 1:10: “Rabbi Redifa said: Rabbi Gasa asked.” Hyman finds no halakhah stated on his own authority, and we find Rabbi Yitzchak bar Redifa: Shabbat 23b.

notes.text: All chapter/halakhah locators in the first part are Jerusalem Talmud. The final Shabbat 23b is Bavli. Hyman’s absence-of-independent-rulings claim remains attributed; no fresh exhaustive search or target identity binding is claimed.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 1:10 reads that Redifa reported Rabbi Nisa’s question, where the supplied Hyman text has Gasa. Both forms are preserved as occurrence-specific readings; a bounded nonmatch in the consulted Peah 4:5 does not establish absence of Hyman’s passage.
